claims.text: The baseline alloy is equimolar CuMoTaWV.
Sputter-deposited equimolar CuMoTaWV can have a nanocrystalline BCC structure.
The intervention is to replace approximately 5 at.% of an unspecified heavier constituent with aluminum.
Minor aluminum substitution will promote in-situ formation of Al2O3 during high-temperature operation.
The resulting Al2O3 will occur as well-dispersed nanoscale precipitates along grain boundaries.
Aluminum will oxidize in a controlled manner at high temperature in the proposed alloy and test environment.
The in-situ alumina precipitates will be stable at the relevant high temperatures.
Alumina precipitates will pin grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary pinning will suppress deleterious grain growth.
The proposed precipitates and grain-boundary pinning will reduce creep.
The aluminum-modified alloy will have at least approximately 10% higher high-temperature yield strength than the aluminum-free baseline.
The aluminum-modified alloy will have better creep resistance than the aluminum-free baseline.
The predicted high-temperature benefit should occur at temperatures of at least 600 degrees Celsius under compressive or tensile loading.
The aluminum-modified alloy will retain room-temperature hardness comparable to the baseline.
The aluminum-modified alloy will retain room-temperature elastic modulus comparable to the baseline.
Replacing a heavier constituent with low-density aluminum will avoid a substantial density increase.
The benefit is restricted to aluminum contents below 10 at.% because higher contents may materially change density or room-temperature properties.
The benefit requires an operating regime that produces controlled alumina without excessive oxidation or phase instability.
